What We Do

Full-Service Pulmonology Revenue Cycle Management

Pulmonology billing combines diagnostic procedure coding for PFTs and bronchoscopy, chronic disease management for COPD and asthma, biologic prior authorization, and DME coordination for CPAP and home ventilators. PMEX manages every element inside your existing pulmonology EHR.

Pulmonary Function Testing

Spirometry (94010), full PFT panel (94060), and diffusion capacity (94729) billed per test.

Bronchoscopy Coding

Diagnostic and therapeutic bronchoscopy codes (31622 to 31654) selected from the report.

CPAP and BiPAP Management

CPAP initiation and management codes billed alongside DME supply coordination.

Biologic Prior Authorization

Dupilumab, mepolizumab, and tezepelumab authorized before each cycle.

Thoracentesis and Pleural Billing

Thoracentesis (32554 to 32557) and chest tube codes billed with imaging guidance add-ons.

Ventilator Management Coding

Hospital ventilator management (94002 to 94004) billed per day of mechanical ventilation.

Sound Familiar?

Common Pulmonology Billing Problems

Each problem below is one PMEX resolves before it costs you revenue.

Full PFT panel billed as spirometry only, losing diffusion capacity and lung volume revenue.

PMEX identifies each PFT component from the test report and bills each separately payable test with the correct CPT code.

Bronchoscopy coded at diagnostic level when a therapeutic procedure was also performed.

PMEX reads the bronchoscopy report and codes the therapeutic procedure when BAL, biopsy, or stent placement is documented.

Asthma biologic prior auth expires mid-cycle, generating retroactive denial on a high-cost drug.

PMEX tracks biologic authorization expiration per patient and initiates renewal 14 days before the next scheduled dose.

Thoracentesis imaging guidance add-on not billed when ultrasound guidance is documented.

PMEX bills 76942 (ultrasound guidance) alongside thoracentesis on every procedure where guidance is documented in the report.

Ventilator management codes not submitted on consecutive hospital days for intubated patients.

PMEX tracks ventilated patients by admission and submits the correct daily ventilator management code for each calendar day of mechanical ventilation.

COPD management visit coded at low complexity when the multi-problem MDM supports higher.

PMEX codes COPD management visits from 2021 MDM criteria, capturing the full complexity of chronic multi-diagnosis management.

Denial Management

Top Denial Patterns in Pulmonology Billing

Pulmonology practices lose 15 to 24 percent of revenue to PFT under-billing, bronchoscopy under-coding, and biologic authorization gaps.

PATTERN 01

PFT Panel Billed as Spirometry Only

Full pulmonary function testing performed: spirometry, lung volumes by plethysmography, diffusion capacity. Only 94010 (spirometry, $45) submitted. 94726 (lung volumes, $80) and 94729 (diffusion capacity, $85) not billed. $165 per PFT panel session not captured.

PMEX SOLUTION

PMEX reviews the PFT report for each test component performed and submits the correct CPT code for every separately billable pulmonary function test: spirometry, lung volumes, diffusion capacity, bronchodilator response, and MVV.

PATTERN 02

Therapeutic Bronchoscopy Billed at Diagnostic Level

Bronchoscopy with BAL and transbronchial biopsy performed. Only 31622 (diagnostic bronchoscopy, $280) submitted. 31628 (bronchoscopy with transbronchial biopsy, $420) is the correct code. $140 per case under-coded when therapeutic procedures are not identified from the report.

PMEX SOLUTION

PMEX reads the bronchoscopy report and selects the CPT code that reflects the highest-complexity procedure performed: diagnostic, with BAL, with biopsy, with stent, or with other interventions as documented.

PATTERN 03

Biologic Authorization Expired, High-Cost Drug Denied

Patient on dupilumab for severe asthma. Commercial prior authorization covers 12 months. Month 13 administered without renewal. Drug claim ($1,800) denied retroactively. Renewal application not initiated before the coverage period ended.

PMEX SOLUTION

PMEX tracks biologic authorization end dates per patient and initiates renewal 14 days before expiration, attaching clinical documentation of asthma control scores and treatment response to every renewal request.
